intro_monologue: Twelve winters on the Thornwick border taught me two habits: grease your buckle-straps before dawn, and never trust a clerk holding a promissory note. The crown stopped paying wages three reorganizations ago, yet the mud still needs holding. Point me at the choke, keep the silver dry, and let's finish before my knees lock up.

intro_monologue: They stripped my sapper commission after a magistrate loaded a watchtower with twice the stone I signed off on, then blamed me when the mortar gave. Fine. Fortresses fail because men ignore load-bearing joints, and shield-walls fail the exact same way. I don't march for songs—I march because shattered walls pay better than intact ones.

intro_monologue: Poaching crown deer in the border woods taught me two useful truths: missing a shot means going hungry, and getting caught means losing a thumb. I kept both thumbs, left the tax-assessors stuck in a peat bog, and discovered military scouting pays twice as much for half the conversation. Keep sixty paces between me and the melee, please.

intro_monologue: Nine years on a wooden toll-platform above the Redmarsh salt-roads taught me to read crosswinds like charcoal tallies. Nobody argued the bridge tariff twice once an ash-shaft pinned their boot to the planks. When bandit companies burned the toll-posts, I took my quiver into the reeds. Game is scarce near the ash-drifts—bounty silver buys better goose-feathers.

intro_monologue: The Capital Collegium expelled me for publishing a monograph proving half the state liturgy consisted of corrupted plumbing diagrams. Field research in Thornvael has been deeply inconvenient: rain warps vellum, blood ruins chalk circles, and mercenaries stand inside blast radii despite explicit warnings. Still, the caldera's ley-drift violates conservation laws—and I intend to measure it.

intro_monologue: I trained in the Thornwick Mint to test silver purity with galvanic arcs, until I proved the treasury was shaving soldiers' pay and blaming my instruments for the variance. Bandit captains conduct lightning far better than clipped coins. Now the caldera vents are shorting out regional ley-currents—and someone has to shut the valve.

intro_monologue: Fourteen years keeping pauper-rolls in Thornwick's lower parish taught me that tax liens outlive their debtors by three generations. When bailiffs demanded I collect from a flooded graveyard, I summoned the signatories directly. They excommunicated me for improper probate procedure—so I brought my bone-awl and brass scales to the front lines where arrears accumulate hourly.

intro_monologue: Raised in a coastal scriptorium witnessing deathbed wills for sailors, I learned early that an oath spoken over salt and bone outlasts the lungs that uttered it. When magistrates forged wills to seize widows' cottages, I summoned dead testators to cross-examine them in court. Now thousands of sworn watchmen lie un-released across Thornvael—and I am here to witness their discharge.
